Bangalore is a cosmopolitan city in India, known for its thriving IT industry and 
innovation hub. It is often referred to as the Silicon Valley of India. Bangalore city is 
home to many multinational companies, startups, research institutes, NGOs, etc. 
that provide internships and placements to students. Bengaluru will soothe you with 
its pleasant weather throughout the year.  
Bangalore is home to several prestigious universities and colleges that offer 
undergraduate and postgraduate courses in a wide range of fields, including arts, 
science, commerce, law, management, and engineering.  
Bangalore has a vibrant campus life that provides students with opportunities for 
learning, networking, cultural exchange, and extracurricular activities. The city is 
also known for its rich cultural heritage and attractions such as garde ns, parks, 
temples, and museums.  
Compared to other metro cities in India, Bangalore has a low cost of living and a 
pleasant climate throughout the year. It is well -connected by road, rail, and air to 
other parts of the country and the world.  
Bangalore is listed as the top 10 fastest growing cities in the world, the economy of 
this city is an important part of the economy of India.

STUDY  ABROAD/EXCHANGE  APPLICATION  AND ADMISSION  
Application documents (in English): 
▪ Completed application form 
▪ Academic transcripts of record (official, stamped and signed by home institution) 
▪ Passport copy (valid for a minimum of six months beyond the date of intended 
departure from India)  
▪ All non-native English speaking applicants must provide proof of English language 
ability or a letter from the home university certifying applicant proficiency 
▪ Proof of international health insurance 
 
INSTRUCTION OF NOMINATION 
Students must be nominated by their home institution’s Advisor/Coordinator. Once 
approved by the home institution, students’ nomination should be sent via email by 
the Advisor/Coordinator to the respective region in charge officers stated below 
with the following information. 
• First Name 
• Last Name 
• Class Level 
• Date of Birth 
• Email ID 
• Program of Study 
 
 
After home institution nomination the prospective exchange students are requested to 
send the completed application form with required documents to:

FEES  
As an Incoming exchange student,  you will pay tuition fees to your  home institution 
based on their fee  requirements. However, exchange students shall pay for things 
such as books and equipment, health insurance, local excursion , accommodation, 
flight, and a student visa. 
 
ACCOMMODATION  
As soon as you have been accepted a course (s) offered from us, you can request 
for off -campus accommodation and Presidency University will facilitate incoming 
students in finding accommodation  close to the campus , approximately 7 -10 kms. 
Students are advised to apply for accommodation as soon as possible after  
accepting an offer letter; so, you have accommodation arranged before your arrival 
in Bangalore, India.  
Note: The university will provide a bus service for all incoming exchange students 
from partner universities so that they can commute to and from campus. 
 
Residence Facilities: 
▪ Twin sharing bedroom (Euro 300 approx. per month) 
▪ Furnished with beds, wardrobes, study tables chairs, bookshelves 
▪ Fan 
▪ Common bathroom toilet 
▪ Wi-Fi

CHOOSING MODULES/COURSES  
You may take courses across multiple faculties (subject to availability, no guarantees 
may be given) as long as your course choices are approved by your home university  
and meet your degree requirements.  Most courses are open to Incoming Exchange 
students. However, some have prerequisites or require permission from the relevant 
faculty or school before you can enroll in them. Students to enroll prior to their arrival 
at Presidency University. However, courses need t o be finalized within one week of 
start of   the class. All the programmes/courses are taught completely in English.  
ACADEMIC WORKLOAD  
Exchange students can take a workload of 12 to 20 credits. The minimum 
workload is 12 credits  and maximum would be 20 credits.  It may be considered on 
the request of the home university on reducing the workload. 
PU 01 credit = U.S. 01 credit. 
PU 01 credit is 15 teaching contact hours (study period, project, assignments, and 
examination period is excluded) 
ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENTS  
A student must have a minimum of 75%  attendance of the classes actually 
conducted in that academic term, for which course(s) the student has registered for 
in the academic term, will be permitted to write the final examination.

TRANSCRIPTS  
All credit-bearing exchange students will be issued with a transcript detailing their  
modules and final grades at the end of the semester, once the exam results have  
been finalized. Transcript’s will be mailed directly to the home university. 
 
WHEN SHOULD YOU ARRIVE  
You should arrive at least 7  days prior to the commencement of the term. Late 
arrival may be accepted under certain conditions such as health or travel/diplomatic 
restrictions.  
VISA  AND IMMIGRATION  REQUIREMENTS  
All international students applying to study in India must have a valid student visa 
(before travelling to India) unless they have an alternative visa that enables them 
to study  in India . If you are granted a student visa, you must comply with all 
student visa conditions. For all visa enquiries and applications, please contact your 
local Indian Embassy/High Commission/Consulate General of India . The visa must 
be valid for the orientation days before the start of the semester. Find more details 
by visiting https://www.mea.gov.in/    
INSURANCE  
All international students  are required to acquire a  health insurance from their  
home country before their  departure. The insurance  should cover for medical  and 
evacuation expenses abroad due to accident or  sickness for the entire  duration of 
exchange at the host country. 
FOREIGN REGIONAL REGISTRATION OFFICES  (FRRO)  
Foreigner visiting India on Student Visa(S) is required to get himself / herself 
registered with concerned FRRO, within 14 days of his/her first arrival, irrespective 
of the duration of his / her stay. FORM –S (Foreign Students Information System) is 
used to capture information about foreign nationals admitted in Indian educational 
institutions. Follow the FRRO link for more details.

SERVICES and SUPPORT 
Studying overseas is a rewarding opportunity to broaden your experience and 
outlook, but it can also be challenging. PU provides the support you need to 
develop academic and professional skills, feel confident in your study and maintain 
your wellbeing. 
PU INTERNATIONAL OFFICE 
The PU International team offers you advice and support during the application 
process and throughout your studies at PU. Our student advisers/Mentors can assist 
with general enquiries, and will keep you up to - date with important news and 
events around PU via emails.

SAFETY AND SECURITY 
PU fosters a safe and secure environment for students, staff and visitors, with 24 -
hour security assistance on and around campus. This includes accessible security 
officers, regular patrols, and closed-circuit television cameras. 
ARRIVAL TIPS 
Students to arrive in Bangalore 7 days prior to start of the formal classes so as to 
finalize the courses and to settle in their accommodation. 
PU International Office offers a complimentary airport shuttle service from 
Bengaluru International Airport to PU for exchange students who arrive 7 days 
before Orientation begins.  Exchange students need to provide their flights details 
and visa for arrange the pick service from the Bengaluru Airport. 
GENERAL SUPPORT SERVICES 
PU provides a wide range of on-campus services for students, including: 
• Medical services 
• Counselling services 
• Accessibility services for students with a disability or ongoing medical 
condition 
• Wi-Fi facility throughout campus 
• Library services 
• Sports facilities 
• Student welfare services 
• Canteen facilities 
• PU Buddy 
• ATM
